description: Character portrait/capture configurations for each capture context (character select, story select, versus ally/enemy, free battle, customize). Selects the animation rows, montage keys, shikigami and weapon montages used by AGameCharacterCaptureActor to pose characters for UI scene captures.

ID.technical: FName primary key of the row (ImportKeyField=Id in the export). FindCharacterCaptureRow walks the resolved CharacterCaptureSet's Id_CharacterCapture list and calls UDataTable::FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CharacterCapture>(CaptureId) on each table; a None id or missing row ends the walk without returning a capture.

CaptureType.simple: Which UI capture context this row configures.
CaptureType.technical: EGameCharacterCaptureType (uint8; None, CharacterSelect, StoryCharacterSelect, VsAlly, VsEnemy, FreeBattle, PvEEquipment, PvEGrowth, Customize, Archive, FreeBattleImage, CP_270_TagCombo, Max, Invalid). The finder compares the row value to the requested slot type and returns the first match in the set; the slot type is converted to a widget capture mask by AGameWidgetManager::ToWidgetCaptureMask. For the pose-driven types (IsSituationOverviewCapture, i.e. the VsAlly/VsEnemy/Customize widget mask bits), several row fields below are bypassed in favour of SituationOverview/SituationOverviewPose rows. Default construction sets None. Exported rows use CharacterSelect (29), StoryCharacterSelect (29), VsAlly (29), VsEnemy (45), FreeBattle (29) and Customize (29).

Id_CharacterAnimation.simple: CharacterAnimationDataTable row holding this capture's montage keys.
Id_CharacterAnimation.technical: FName joined to CharacterAnimationDataTables (DTM +0x4A0). For non-pose captures GetCharacterAnimationMap resolves this row and keeps only entries whose Key equals CharacterIdleAnimationKey or CharacterEnterAnimationKey, mapping Key -> FileName (montage asset name); entries with a None key or file are skipped. For SituationOverview captures the pose's Id_CharacterAnimation_Ally/Enemy row is used instead, so this field is not read on that path. Missing row yields an empty map; later idle/enter playback uses FindChecked on the key.

CharacterIdleAnimationKey.simple: Animation key selecting the idle montage for this capture.
CharacterIdleAnimationKey.technical: FName added to the two-key filter list used against the CharacterAnimation row's Key/FileName arrays; the mapped file name is resolved through the slot's AnimMontageLoaders and played by AnimInstance::Montage_Play (play rate 1, MontageLength return type, stop existing montages). PlayIdleMontage uses FindChecked, so a missing key/file is an unchecked lookup. Ignored on SituationOverview pose captures, which play the pose animation row's FileName[0].

CharacterEnterAnimationKey.simple: Animation key selecting the entrance montage for this capture.
CharacterEnterAnimationKey.technical: FName used exactly like CharacterIdleAnimationKey but by PlayEnterMontage; that function returns early for SituationOverview captures. The resolved montage is also stored as Slot.Montage. Typical exported values are <Context>_Enter.

Id_ShikigamiCharacter.simple: Shikigami character to spawn alongside the captured character.
Id_ShikigamiCharacter.technical: FName joined to ShikigamiDataTables (DTM +0x6C0). None means no shikigami: SpawnShikigami returns, the shikigami animation map is empty and shikigami montage playback is skipped. Otherwise the Shikigami row's FileName_BP is loaded as an AGameShikigami (Character-primary asset loader), set up, positioned, given material parameters and a capture-only visible mesh. A missing Shikigami row aborts LoadCharacter entirely for the slot.

ShikigamiDefaultMaterialPattern.simple: Material pattern index applied to the captured shikigami.
ShikigamiDefaultMaterialPattern.technical: int32 passed directly as the Pattern argument of Shikigami->GetMaterialController()->SetMaterialPattern(Pattern, nullptr); the null Row pointer means no explicit CharacterMaterial row is used at this call. Default construction sets 0; many exported rows use 0, with non-zero values on shikigami-specific captures. Only affects the spawned shikigami, not the captured character (whose pattern comes from slot/variation parameters).

Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation.simple: ShikigamiAnimationDataTable row holding the shikigami's capture montage keys.
Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation.technical: FName joined to ShikigamiAnimationDataTables (DTM +0x6E0). For non-pose captures GetShikigamiAnimationMap resolves this row and filters its Key/FileName arrays by the two shikigami animation keys below; missing row yields an empty map (and later FindChecked can fail). For SituationOverview captures the pose's Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation_Ally/Enemy row replaces this field. Only consulted when Id_ShikigamiCharacter is non-None.

ShikigamiCharacterIdleAnimationKey.simple: Animation key selecting the shikigami's idle montage.
ShikigamiCharacterIdleAnimationKey.technical: FName used to filter the ShikigamiAnimation row into Key -> FileName and then FindChecked on the resulting map in PlayShikigamiIdleMontage; the resolved montage is played on the shikigami's AnimInstance. Returns early when no shikigami was spawned or Id_ShikigamiCharacter is None; pose captures use the pose animation row instead.

ShikigamiCharacterEnterAnimationKey.simple: Animation key selecting the shikigami's entrance montage.
ShikigamiCharacterEnterAnimationKey.technical: FName used like the shikigami idle key in PlayShikigamiEnterMontage, which also returns early for SituationOverview captures. Requires a valid spawned shikigami AnimInstance and a non-None Id_ShikigamiCharacter.

Id_AnimationWeapon.simple: Weapon IDs whose montages are loaded for this capture (parallel to the two animation-name arrays).
Id_AnimationWeapon.technical: TArray<FName>, typically two slots. For every non-None entry, GetWeaponAnimationNames adds WeaponIdleAnimationName[i] and WeaponEnterAnimationName[i] to the slot's AnimMontage loader list (animation asset names, not the weapon assets themselves). The IDs are also tested against attached weapon actor names: GetWeaponFileNamePrefix(AttachName, false) takes the leading 'WP_000' length (6 chars) and a case-insensitive StartsWith test selects the row index. In non-pose captures, the count of non-None entries that have a non-None idle name also forces spawned weapons onto the 'root' socket instead of the CharacterWeapon socket. SituationOverview pose captures use the pose row's Id_AnimationWeapon_Ally/Enemy instead of this field for montage playback.

WeaponIdleAnimationName.simple: Montage asset name played on an attached weapon's skeletal mesh for the idle pose.
WeaponIdleAnimationName.technical: TArray<FName> indexed by Id_AnimationWeapon. Non-None names at non-None weapon slots are added to the AnimMontage primary-asset loaders. PlayWeaponIdleMontages matches the attached weapon prefix (case-insensitive 'WP_000' prefix), FindChecked's the loader by this name, then calls OverrideAnimationData(montage, true, true, 0, 1) and PlayAnimation(montage, true). A non-None count also makes SpawnCharacter attach such weapons at socket 'root' for non-pose captures.

WeaponEnterAnimationName.simple: Montage asset name played on an attached weapon's skeletal mesh for the entrance pose.
WeaponEnterAnimationName.technical: TArray<FName> indexed by Id_AnimationWeapon. Preloaded next to the idle name for every non-None weapon id; PlayWeaponEnterMontages repeats the prefix match, loader FindChecked, OverrideAnimationData and PlayAnimation. Not used on SituationOverview captures (there the pose row's WeaponAnimationName_Ally/Enemy supplies the names).

notes: Export contains 190 rows. Lookup is character -> Character::Id_CharacterCapture -> CharacterCaptureSet row -> first CharacterCapture row whose CaptureType matches the requested slot type; a None id or missing row stops the search.

For VsAlly, VsEnemy and certain Customize widget-capture slots (IsSituationOverviewCapture), montage and weapon selections come from CharacterRow::Id_SituationOverview -> SituationOverviewPose rows (Ally for VsAlly, Enemy otherwise); the CharacterCapture row's animation-related fields are then largely bypassed. This split is why many exported VsAlly/VsEnemy rows have None animation fields.
Montage and weapon loader names are staged as Character-primary assets by LoadCharacter; missing rows can abort the slot before any asset loader is created.
The row constructor explicitly defaults CaptureType to None and ShikigamiDefaultMaterialPattern to 0 (retail TCppStructOps::Construct 0x16c5650 inlined).
Evidence is reconstructed source with retail RVA comments; no claim is made about byte-identical matching, Blueprint-only callers, or retail assets not present in the partial Content export.

usages.detail: FindCharacterCaptureRow walks Character -> CharacterCaptureSet -> CharacterCapture and matches on CaptureType.
SpawnShikigami applies ShikigamiDefaultMaterialPattern through the shikigami material controller.
LoadCharacter resolves the capture row and collects character, shikigami, montage and weapon loader names.
GetCharacterAnimationMap filters the CharacterAnimation row by idle/enter keys.
GetShikigamiAnimationMap filters the ShikigamiAnimation row by shikigami idle/enter keys.
GetWeaponAnimationNames collects idle and enter weapon montage names per non-None weapon slot.
PlayIdleMontage resolves CharacterIdleAnimationKey to a loaded montage and plays it.
PlayWeaponIdleMontages matches attached weapon prefixes against Id_AnimationWeapon and plays the idle montage.
PlayWeaponEnterMontages does the same for the entrance montage.
